headline: City officials presented the Flock Safety camera program, covering search access, data sharing, and seven-day data retention.
summary: City officials presented a review of the Flock Safety camera program and how the system works. The presentation said 27 superior officers and 10 detectives can search the system, and each search requires a lawful reason and a dispatcher-issued case number. Councillor McDonald asked whether Flock may use city data for company-wide analysis, and Chief Gatcomb agreed to respond.

This evening's presentation began with an opening statement from Chief Gatcomb and then an online screen presentation on the Flock camera system and demonstration on how it works. The entirety of the presentation may be viewed on the Urban Media Arts You Tube page at https://www.youtube.com/live/pAqsXUr2PQk?

si=TfPU4v0FtQBqxWwu. The presentation is also attached to the history of this paper.

Of the MPD staff, only 27 superior officers and 10 detectives have access to be able to search the system, all must require a lawful reason and dispatcher issued case number when doing so. There are a limited amount of cities that are allowed to share data with Malden when investigating crimes. For every search, there is a breadcrumb trail and accessibility audit to account for who and why the searches are being conducted. Search data held in Malden is only retained for seven days.

Councillor McDonald asked Chief Gatcomb if he would ask the Flock company if they have the ability to use any of their cities data for any type of company wide analysis and if the company's terms of use allow for such data collection. Chief Gatcomb confirmed he would respond back with an answer to the Councillor's question.

## 5. ADJOURNMENT

A motion was made by Councillor McDonald, seconded by Councillor O'Malley, that this meeting be adjourned. The motion carried unanimously. Meeting was adjourned at 8:55 PM.
